Eligibility  | Inclusion Criteria: - Is male or female and =55 and =95 years of age living in the community or in an institutionalized setting - Meets clinical criteria for possible or probable AD based on the 2011 National Institute on Aging-Alzheimer Association (NIA-AA) criteria - Meets the revised criteria for psychosis in major or mild neurocognitive disorder established by the International Psychogeriatrics Association (IPA) - Has either blood-based biomarker or documented evidence (e.g. positron emission tomography, cerebrospinal fluid biomarker) indicating amyloid plaque deposition and neuropathologic change consistent with AD - Has a prior magnetic resonance imaging or computed tomography scan of the brain that is consistent with the diagnosis of AD - Meets revised criteria for psychosis in major or mild neurocognitive disorder as per International Psychogeriatrics Association - MMSE score =6 and =24 - Psychotic symptoms for at least 2 months - Lives in a stable place of residence and there are no plans to change living arrangements - Has a designated study partner/caregiver - Able to complete all study visits with a study partner/caregiver - Must be on a stable dose of cholinesterase inhibitor or memantine, if applicable Exclusion Criteria: - Requires treatment with a medication prohibited by the protocol - Is in hospice and receiving end-of-life palliative care, or has become bedridden - Requires skilled nursing care - Psychotic symptoms that are primarily attributable to delirium, substance abuse, or a medical or psychiatric condition other than dementia - Known history of cerebral amyloid angiopathy, epilepsy, central nervous system neoplasm, or unexplained syncope - Atrial fibrillation - Symptomatic orthostatic hypotension - Protocol-defined exclusionary clinical laboratory findings Additional inclusion/exclusion criteria apply.

## Study Overview

Brief Summary

This clinical trial is a Phase 2/3 study that will determine the recommended dose and dose regimen of AG-236 and evaluate the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of AG-236 in polycythemia vera (PV) by testing how well AG-236 works compared to placebo to increase the number of subjects with no phlebotomy and absence of phlebotomy eligibility over a 13-week period. In addition, the long-term effect of AG-236 on efficacy and safety will be explored in an open-label extension portion.

Detailed Description

AG-236 is a small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA) targeting transmembrane serine protease 6 (TMPRSS6) intended for the treatment of PV. The study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of treatment with AG-236 in subjects with PV. The study is a Phase 2/3 study in which the recommended dose and dose regimen of AG-236 will be selected and further evaluated. The Phase 2 portion includes a 26-week randomized, placebo-controlled period in which subjects will be randomized in a 1:1:1:1:1 ratio to receive 1 of 3 dose levels of AG-236 in 1 of 2 dose regimens or placebo. The Phase 3 portion includes a 26-week randomized, placebo-controlled period in which subjects will be randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive the recommended AG-236 dose level and dose regimen or placebo. Subjects who complete either the Phase 2 or Phase 3 portion will have the option to move into a 104-week open-label extension period to receive AG-236.

Official Title

A Phase 2/3, Double-blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter, Efficacy, Safety, and Pharmacokinetics Study of AG-236 in Subjects With Polycythemia Vera

Name

Brief summary

This is a Phase 2b/3 study designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of chronic treatment with brelovitug (a.k.a BJT-778; BTG) for chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection. The comparator in this study will be 24-weeks of delayed treatment. During the 24-weeks of delayed treatment, participants will complete the same visits and assessments as those randomized to initiate brelovitug immediately. At the completion of 24-week delayed treatment period, all participants will start treatment with brelovitug.

Materials & Methods: IZAR-2 (NCT06641089) is a 52-week multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebocontrolled, parallel-group Phase 3 clinical trial of the Nanobody sonelokimab in patients with active PsA and previous inadequate response or intolerance to 1 or 2 biologic TNFi. An estimated 600 adult patients with a confirmed diagnosis of PsA per CASPAR criteria, active disease (68 tender joint count ≥3 and 66 swollen joint count ≥3), currently active or dermatologist-confirmed historical PsO, and inadequate response or intolerance to 1 or 2 biologic TNFi will be enrolled. Patients will be randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive sonelokimab 60mg or 120mg Q4W WI (induction doses at W0, 2, 4, and 6), placebo to W16, or risankizumab given at the approved PsA dose (active reference arm; Figure). The primary outcome is ACR50 vs. placebo at W16, with key secondary outcomes (all vs. placebo) including the proportion of patients achieving ACR20, PASI 90, MDA, as well as change from baseline in the Health Assessment Questionnaire-Disability Index and Short Form-36 Physical Component Summary at W16. Risankizumab, an approved IL-23 p19i therapy commonly used in PsA after prior inadequate response to TNFi, will be the active reference arm. A key secondary endpoint will compare ACR50 responses at W16 with sonelokimab vs. risankizumab to provide additional insights into treatment choice after the failure of TNFi therapies in this population. After W16, patients receiving placebo will switch to sonelokimab 120mg Q4W WI (induction dosing to W24) until the end of treatment at W52. The IZAR-2 trial is ongoing and actively recruiting at sites across Europe and North America. ## Study Overview

Brief Summary

The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the immunogenicity, safety, and immune persistence of the primary series of an investigational group ACYW135 meningococcal conjugate vaccine, as well as the immunogenicity and safety of a booster dose administered at 12 months of age, in healthy children aged 3 to 5 months.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Is the immune response induced by the primary series of the investigational vaccine non-inferior to that of the licensed control vaccine? What is the safety profile of the investigational vaccine during the primary series and booster dose? Does the investigational vaccine provide immune persistence up to 12 months of age? What is the immunogenicity of a booster dose administered at 12 months of age? Researchers will compare the investigational vaccine group with the active comparator group (CanSinoBIO MCV-ACYW) during both the primary immunization phase and the booster phase.

Participants will:

Be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either three doses of the investigational vaccine or three doses of the control vaccine according to a 0,1,2-month schedule during the primary immunization phase; Receive a booster dose at 12 months of age (either investigational vaccine or control vaccine according to group assignment); Provide blood samples at four time points: before primary vaccination, 30 days after primary vaccination, before booster vaccination (12 months of age), and 30 days after booster vaccination; Be observed for 30 minutes after each dose for immediate adverse reactions; Have solicited local and systemic adverse events recorded for 7 days after each dose using diary cards; Have unsolicited adverse events recorded for 30 days after each dose using diary cards; Be monitored for serious adverse events for at least 6 months after the last dose administered; A total of 880 participants will be enrolled.

Official Title

A Randomized, Double-Blind, Active Comparator-Controlled Phase Ⅲ Trial to Evaluate the Immunogenicity and Safety of the Group ACYW135 Meningococcal Conjugate Vaccine in Population Aged 3 to 5 Months

## Oral VK2735 for Weight Management in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Phase 3 (SUNRISE 2)

ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT07868939

Sponsor Viking Therapeutics, Inc.

Information provided by Viking Therapeutics, Inc. (Responsible Party)

Last Update Posted 2026-10-09

Not yet recruiting 

Brief Summary

This study is one of two planned Phase 3 studies to support the weight management indication for VK2735 Oral in obese (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI ≥ 27 kg/m2) adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

Detailed Description

This is a Phase 3, multicenter, 68-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel arm study that will evaluate the weight loss efficacy as well as safety, tolerability, pharmacodynamic effects, and pharmacokinetics of VK2735 oral formulation in adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) who are obese or overweight. Three VK2735 doses and matched placebo administered orally will be evaluated (Group 1 = Placebo; Group 2 = 27.5 mg; Group 3 = 35 mg; Group 4 = 55 mg). All participants in Treatment Groups 2 - 4 will initiate dosing at 10 mg, then increase dose to 17.5 mg at Week 4. The dose will be increased every 4 weeks for each treatment group until Treatment Group 2 reaches 27.5 mg at Week 8, Treatment Group 3 reaches 35 mg at Week 12 and Treatment Group 4 reaches 55 mg at Week 16.

Official Title

A Phase 3 Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, 68-Week Efficacy and Safety Study of VK2735 Administered Orally for Weight Management in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Who Are Obese, or Overweight

# A Study of Telitacicept for the Treatment of Generalized Myasthenia Gravis (UPSTREAM MG)

# Study on Telitacicept for treating generalized myasthenia gravis.

Not Recruiting

18 years and older

All

Phase 3

This study is testing a new treatment for generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG), a disease where the immune system attacks the body's own nerves and muscles, causing weakness. The goal is to see if a medicine called telitacicept can help. Telitacicept is a protein designed to stop certain immune system parts from attacking the body. In this study, some patients will get telitacicept, and others will get a placebo (a dummy treatment) to compare results. It will last for several weeks, including a 4-week screening, a 24-week treatment, and a longer open-label extension period where all participants can receive telitacicept. Participants must be adults with a confirmed diagnosis of gMG. They should not have other autoimmune diseases or recent infections.

  * The study involves a total duration variable, with key periods like 24-week treatment and 48-week open-label extension.
  * Participants must have gMG and meet specific test scores to qualify.
  * It's vital to check for other health issues that might exclude participation.
